# Synthetic aircraft repair manual excerpt for regression tests.

4.3  Fuselage Skin Crack — Field Repair Procedure

1. Inspect the crack
The certified structures technician shall inspect the crack and mark its extent.

2. Remove damaged material
Remove damaged material from the affected area.

3. Grind surface
Grind the surrounding surface to bright metal.

4. Preheat
Before welding, preheat the component to the specified temperature.

5. Apply weld passes
Apply multiple weld passes according to the qualified WPS.

6. Once welding is complete, allow the component to air cool for 30 minutes.

7. Following cooling, perform ultrasonic testing to confirm weld integrity.

8. After ultrasonic testing passes, perform a stress relief heat treatment cycle.

If ultrasonic testing indicates incomplete fusion, repeat steps 5–7 before proceeding to stress relief.

4.5  Engine Mount Bracket Weld Repair

This procedure applies to hairline cracks found on the engine mount bracket during borescope inspection.

This procedure differs from the fuselage skin repair in preheat temperature and inspection method (dye penetrant vs. ultrasonic testing).

1. Inspect the crack region
Inspect the crack region using magnetic particle inspection.

2. Remove damaged material
Remove damaged material from the bracket weld zone.

3. Grind surface
Grind the surface to clean metal.

4. Preheat
Before welding, preheat the bracket to 120°C.

5. Apply weld passes
Apply weld passes per the engine mount repair specification.

6. Perform dye penetrant testing
Perform dye penetrant testing to confirm crack closure.

7. Perform stress relief
Perform stress relief of the repaired bracket weld zone.
